## Kroger Packaged Cheese Sales {#sec-data-kroger-cheese}

These data record weekly sales of packaged, sliced American cheese at Kroger grocery
stores across 11 U.S. cities. They were assembled by James Scott for use as a teaching
dataset in *Data Science in R: A Gentle Introduction*, where they first appear in the
Plots chapter to illustrate exploratory data visualization before being revisited in
later chapters on regression with dummy variables. The data are used throughout to
examine how price and in-store promotional displays relate to cheese sales volume.

**Resources:**

- [Data Science in R: A Gentle Introduction](https://bookdown.org/jgscott/DSGI/)

**Provenance.** The data were compiled by James Scott (University of Texas at Austin)
for instructional use and distributed with *Data Science in R: A Gentle Introduction*
(bookdown, last updated August 2021). The dataset covers 11 U.S. cities — Atlanta,
Birmingham, Cincinnati, Columbus, Dallas, Detroit, Houston, Indianapolis, Louisville,
Nashville, and Roanoke — with 706 observations. No formal license is stated; the data
are made available for educational use through the book's online companion. See
@kroger-cheese for the primary citation.

### Variables {.unnumbered}

| Variable | Type | Unit / Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vol` | Continuous | packages, 799–14,534 | Sales volume in packages of packaged, sliced American cheese. Serves as the outcome variable in regression analyses. |
| `price` | Continuous | USD, 1.72–3.83 | Retail price charged per package. Key predictor of sales volume. |
| `disp` | Binary | yes / no | Whether a promotional in-store display was shown during the observation period. Coded as a character variable ("yes" / "no"). |
| `city` | Categorical | 11 cities | City in which the Kroger store is located (Atlanta, Birmingham, Cincinnati, Columbus, Dallas, Detroit, Houston, Indianapolis, Louisville, Nashville, Roanoke). |
